question: A 58-year-old patient was admitted for septic shock. After 5 days he is haemodynamically stable on low-dose noradrenaline, self-ventilating on 2 L/min nasal cannula O2 with SpO2 96%, oriented to time and place, and taking sips of water. Which action is MOST appropriate?

answers.text: Continue ICU care until vasopressor is fully weaned before considering step-down

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Full vasopressor weaning is desirable but not mandatory before step-down; improving trajectory and stable observations support transfer to HDU while continuing low-dose vasopressor.

answers.text: Plan step-down to a High-Dependency Unit (HDU) with continued monitoring and vasopressor weaning

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This patient meets step-down criteria: haemodynamic improvement on minimal support, adequate oxygenation, intact mentation, and oral tolerance. HDU allows continued monitoring during the final vasopressor wean.

answers.text: Discharge directly to a general ward given clinical improvement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Direct ICU-to-ward discharge is unsafe while the patient still requires a vasopressor; ICU bounce-back risk is high. Step-down to HDU is the safer intermediate step.

answers.text: Perform a weaning trial with planned extubation before considering discharge

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The patient is already self-ventilating — he is not intubated. This option is not applicable here.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the ICU discharge criteria: improving physiological trajectory, single-organ or no vasopressor support acceptable for step-down, adequate oxygenation, and intact mentation. HDU bridges the gap between ICU and general ward.
Excellent. Structured step-down to HDU is the standard for patients who are improving but still require monitoring and minimal organ support.
